fallos_mitigaciones: Untrained (NFT) memory model Mtheta generates redundant/harmful memory that DEGRADES SE performance (Tab.1-2, e.g. Devstral+DeepSeek-1.5B SR down3.50pp/down6.00pp cross-episode); mitigated via trajectory-based rejection sampling (Alg.1, Eq.1 S3.2) that filters candidate memories failing the acceptance criterion (for-all-i delta_i>=0 AND exists-i delta_i>0) before SFT/RL training of the memory model.
cita: Guo et al. (2026). Enhancing Software Engineering Through Closed-Loop Memory Optimization.
notes: S2.1/A.2: memory Mk stored in a single markdown file Memory.md, integrating 'lessons learned, codebase structures identified, reasoning patterns discovered, and task-relevant contextual information' -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA;PROCEDIMENTAL, representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (A.2 preliminary study: 9 candidate structures tested -- String/Dict/List/Tree/Graph/Python/Given/Discretionary/Ours -- Ours=markdown wins Table3, dAbs>=17.65% LA(-1), Table3). S2.3/S2.1 cross-episode Mk=Mtheta(R,S(Mk-1,tau_k)) combines prior memory+new trajectory each task completion -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (after task Tk completes). retrieval=NA: whole Memory.md is injected wholesale into agent context, no ranking/embedding/graph search component described. mide_lectura=SI: the entire MemOp framework defines memory utility as causal downstream impact -- S2.2 Eq.1 measures Delta_i(Mj) vs no-memory baseline across NQ=10 metrics (SR/LA/Eresolve/LE), i.e. it directly measures the utility of READING/using generated memory during task-solving -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=PROYECTO: Alg.1 samples NT tasks per repository R and cross-episode memory accumulates 'repository-level shared knowledge base' within the same repo (S3.4/S4.2). Table6/Fig.22 (F.3 Computation Overhead): API cost per-100-instances ($11.73-$86.18 construction), Delta_rel>=9.79% total computational cost reduction (abstract, S4.2) -> metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. A.2 Table3 ablates 9 memory-structure variants vs no-memory baseline + Fig.4 ablates SFT-only vs SFT+RL training stages -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Tables1-2 SWE-bench-Verified single/cross-episode results (up-to-5.25% SR, 4.63% Eresolve gains) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. F_screening was WRITE;COSTO (abstract-only); confirmed against full text adds CONSOLIDACION (cross-episode memory evolution S2.3), RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (utility-of-reading is the paper's core contribution), PROCEDIMENTAL (memory encodes reasoning/debugging patterns, not just facts), and NEGATIVO(b) (NFT-Mtheta/naive memory consistently HURTS SE performance, Tab.1-2, motivating the trained/validated memory design).

fallos_mitigaciones: Context pollution: raw/irrelevant retrieved experiences 'waste tokens and distract the agent' (S3.1); mitigated via TF-IDF similarity threshold tau_sim + top-1-only retrieval + structured abstraction (task_description/execution_summary/confidence fields, only SUCCESSFUL trajectories retained) instead of raw traces. Table3 (RQ2): Naive-EET (raw trajectory context, no abstraction) only reaches -26.0% cost / -3.1% resolved vs EET's -31.8% cost / +2.7% resolved, confirming structured abstraction beats raw memory injection.
cita: Guo et al. (2026). EET: Experience-Driven Early Termination for Cost-Efficient Software Engineering Agents.
notes: S3.1: each resolved issue is distilled into a structured experience object (task_description/execution_summary/evaluation_result=pass-only/confidence/confidence_reason) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(per-issue trajectory)+PROCEDIMENTAL(actionable debugging/stopping signals), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS. operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION: 'we retain only high-quality experience... evaluation_result field is set to pass for all stored experiences' (S3.1) = explicit success-only admission filter. trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (experience generated after each historical issue resolution completes). retrieval=RANKING: TF-IDF text-similarity of task_description against experience base, threshold tau_sim, top-1 only (S3.1). mide_lectura=SI: S5.3 RQ3 ablation w/o-experience-injection drops resolution rate by 10.4pp despite cutting cost a further 30.7% (Table4) -- direct causal measurement of the utility of READING retrieved experience -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=ORGANIZACION: experience base built from SWE-bench-Lite (207 tasks, many repos) is applied cross-repository to SWE-bench-Verified issues (500 tasks, different repos); explicit zero-repository-overlap transfer check (Trae Agent, 50 issues) still cuts cost $12.7->$9.6 at matched 14.0% SR (S5.1/App.F), i.e. experience generalizes beyond a single project. Table1: EET cuts total cost 19.3%-55.1% (avg 31.8%) across 6 agent x backend configs with resolution-rate loss <=0.2% (some configs +7.8%/+7.2%); Table2 early-termination rate avg 11.3% of issues. F_screening was COSTO only; full text confirms/adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (RQ3 ablation), PROCEDIMENTAL (experience captures reusable debugging patterns per S5.1 cross-repo transfer discussion).

fallos_mitigaciones: Graph-based LTM (Graphiti, cognee) accuracy gap vs vector/full-context is 'driven by retrieval incompleteness rather than reasoning failure' (Table III: cognee/Graphiti 25.58-28.18% 'unknown' responses vs 8.38-11.14% for mem0/RAG/full-context) -- a structural retrieval-coverage weakness the paper measures but does not itself mitigate (pure evaluation study).
cita: Wolff and Bennati (2026). Cost and Accuracy of Long-Term Memory in Distributed Multi-Agent Systems Based on Large Language Models.
notes: Pure independent testbed/benchmark paper (no own memory mechanism) -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA per rule5; it MEASURES accuracy (LLM-as-judge, majority-of-3) + system-level cost (CPU/RAM/disk/network/TCO) of three 3rd-party LTM frameworks -- mem0 (vector), Graphiti (graph), cognee (hybrid) -- plus RAG and full-context baselines, on all ten LoCoMo conversations (1,540 QA pairs) under unconstrained vs constrained (150ms latency/512KB-s bandwidth/30ms jitter) simulated cloud-edge network (SIII Method/Operation). Table III: mem0 highest at 81.08% accurate, RAG 78.31%, full-context 77.16%, Graphiti 56.03%, cognee 55.27%. mide_lectura=SI (accuracy IS the primary read-quality metric) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. Table IV per-category breakdown includes a Temporal question category (mem0 55.48% highest, Graphiti 31.83% lowest) = a staleness/knowledge-update-adjacent axis explicitly reported -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. alcance=SESION: LoCoMo's up-to-32-session multi-session dialogues are the unit of study; 'Memory backends are logically wiped between conversations' (Threats-to-Validity/Internal) confirming per-conversation/session scope, not cross-project accumulation. multiagente=NO despite 'Distributed Multi-Agent Systems' framing in the title/abstract: the DMAS label refers to the distributed EDGE/CLOUD deployment topology of pipeline components (coordinator/responder/memory service, toxiproxy) simulating network constraints, NOT memory shared across multiple distinct AI agents with separate goals -- matches F_screening's absence of a MULTIAGENTE tag. TCO/Pareto: 'RAG matches the upper cluster at 8.4 times lower total cost of ownership than mem0, and both are the only non-dominated backends on the Pareto frontier' (abstract/Fig.2) -> COSTO in F, MEDICION-COSTO. NEGATIVO(b): 'full-context forwarding underperforms mem0 despite supplying the entire conversation for each question' (abstract) = negative evidence that naive maximal-context 'memory' does not guarantee better accuracy than a compressed/precise memory design. F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds FIDELIDAD + NEGATIVO.

benchmarks: Amazon Books, Amazon Goodreads, MovieTV, Yelp (InstructRec splits)
fallos_mitigaciones: Cognitive Overload: naively injecting raw neighbor memories 'bombards the LLM with noise, resulting in hallucinations and diminished instruction adherence' (S2.1.1); mitigated via Information-Bottleneck-inspired 'Curate-then-Synthesize' (LLM-generated domain curation rules R_domain prune neighbors Eq.1-2, then LM_Mem synthesizes distilled confidence-scored facets Eq.3). Prohibitive Collaborative Updates: naive synchronous propagation scales O(|N'k|) LLM calls with redundant repeated user-context tokens per neighbor; mitigated via Asynchronous Collaborative Propagation batching self-reflection+neighbor updates into one call, achieving O(1) call complexity (S2.1.3, Eq.5-6).
cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemRec: Collaborative Memory-Augmented Agentic Recommender System.
notes: S2.1: unified collaborative memory graph G=(V,E), V=UsersuItems, each node stores an evolving semantic memory Mv -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA, representacion=GRAFO. S2.1.1 Collaborative Memory Retrieval: zero-shot LLM-as-Rule-Generator curates top-k' neighbors via domain-adaptive multiplier rules (Eq.1-2, Fig.3) then LM_Mem synthesizes them into structured preference facets Mcollab with a confidence score + explicit 'Supporting Neighbors' evidence list per facet (Eq.3, Fig.4-5) -> retrieval=GRAFO;RANKING, and the confidence+cited-neighbor-evidence design is a genuine provenance/grounding mechanism -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F ('Grounding the reasoning in Mcollab ensures that the generated rationale is factually supported by broader community evidence', S2.1.2). S2.1.3 Async Collaborative Propagation triggered per new user-item interaction event (Eq.5-6) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA, operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION. mide_lectura=SI: S3.3 RQ2 explicitly ablates architectural decoupling vs a Naive Collaborative Agent (uncurated raw context, single-stage) -- Naive plateaus from information bottleneck while MemRec gains +34% relative H@1 on Books (Fig.6) -- directly measures the utility of curated READING -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F, evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Tables 2-3: MemRec beats all baselines (LightGCN/SASRec/P5/Vanilla-LLM/iAgent/RecBot/AgentCF/i2Agent) on all 4 datasets, p<0.05, e.g. Goodreads H@1 +28.98% -> BENCHMARK-E2E. S3.4 RQ3 online-inference cost/latency Pareto analysis across deployment configs -> COSTO in F, MEDICION-COSTO. alcance=ORGANIZACION: Table1 shows one shared graph spans 3K-12K users x 30K-121K items per dataset (whole-community scope, not per-project/session). multiagente=NO: 'collaborative' here means collaborative-filtering signal sharing ACROSS USERS/ITEMS on one graph, not multiple distinct AI agents sharing memory (single LM_Mem + single LLM_Rec pipeline) -- matches F_screening's absence of a MULTIAGENTE tag. F_screening was WRITE;COSTO; full text confirms and adds CONSOLIDACION, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

benchmarks: HNSW (FAISS) comparison on synthetic 'Dense Forest' dataset (own, D=768, N in 10^4-10^6)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Vector Haze': Flat-RAG/bag-of-embeddings architectures retrieve 'semantically similar but episodically disjointed facts that confuse rather than aid the agent' (S1/S2.1); mitigated via the Atlas hierarchical spatial index constraining search to the agent's active context region plus the Trace episodic DAG providing temporal/causal structure (S3.6).
cita: Arslan (2026). Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents.
notes: Pure systems/engineering paper with ZERO downstream task-accuracy evaluation (no SWE-bench/LoCoMo/QA benchmark; only micro/macro latency-throughput-compression benchmarks on a synthetic 'Dense Forest' D=768 dataset + an HNSW/FAISS comparison, S5-6) -> mide_lectura=NO (measures retrieval SPEED, never retrieval CORRECTNESS/utility), so RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO is correctly excluded from F. S3.2 Atlas = SIMD-accelerated INT8-quantized spatial vector index (semantic concepts) + S3.6 Trace = neuro-symbolic episodic DAG (TraceEvent nodes Vuser/Vsystem/Vconcept, temporal Enext + reference Eref edges into Atlas) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA, representacion=HIBRIDA (vector+graph). operaciones=WRITE;OLVIDO: S3.3 WAL insert path + S3.4 Sidecar Blob Arena (append-only, generational GC discarding tombstoned/dead blobs) + S6.9 Trace GC (compaction, tombstone scan). This is STORAGE-level garbage collection/eviction (OLVIDO), NOT content-level summarization/merging of memory (no CONSOLIDACION mechanism found anywhere in the text: grep for consolidat/summar/dedup/merge in the full PDF returns nothing beyond GC/tombstone terminology) -- corrects F_screening's CONSOLIDACION tag, which appears to have been an abstract-only misread of 'generational garbage collection'. trigger=NA: the paper never specifies a concrete policy for WHEN a new semantic concept gets allocated/written (abstracted away to the Python 'Shell' managing 'LLM interaction, prompt engineering', S3.1) nor when compaction runs (GC-ratio=0.5 appears only as an evaluation-harness setting, S6.9), so this axis is genuinely undefined. S4.2.1 Multi-Tenant Isolation: SLB sharded 64-way by hash(session_id), 'Session A will never evict or access cache entries from Session B', scaling to >100,000 concurrent sessions on one node -> alcance=SESION, multiagente=NO (explicit ISOLATION, i.e. the opposite of sharing, matches F_screening's absent MULTIAGENTE tag), and this cross-tenant leakage prevention is itself a memory-security design choice -> SEGURIDAD in F. Table2/Fig.1: INT8 SDOT 4.70ns vs FP32 26.5ns (5.6x), 3.1x on-disk compression, WAL overhead <1% (Table4, within measurement noise), P99 EBR read latency 750ns under 16-thread contention -> COSTO in F, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO;ABLATION (WAL on/off Table4, FP32-vs-INT8 Table2-3, flat-vs-Atlas Fig.4, beam=1/3/3+CSLS Table5).

fallos_mitigaciones: Offline query-agnostic memory construction ('build once, use always') is 'wasteful' (spends computation regardless of query need) and 'brittle' (irreversible preprocessing may discard query-critical information, S1); mitigated via runtime on-demand extraction that keeps raw history intact (never offline-processed) and defers processing until query time, combined with an explicit RL-trained cost-aware budget-tier router (Eq.7-10) that trades task performance against extraction cost per module.
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory.
notes: S3-4: BudgetMem performs RUNTIME on-demand memory extraction m=f_mem(q,Cq) over a STATIC raw chunk store C that is never offline-processed (S3 'Inputs': 'This step only segments raw text for indexing and does not perform any offline extraction, summarization, or rewriting') -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(entity/temporal/topic facts+summary, Eq.4-6);TRABAJO(memory m is rebuilt fresh per query, not persisted for reuse), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS(text chunks/structured fields/NL notes). operaciones=NA: no WRITE/ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION of a persistent memory store is defined -- the mechanism is query-triggered on-demand EXTRACTION+ROUTING over an immutable chunk store, which the RQ2 operaciones vocabulary does not cover. retrieval=EMBEDDINGS: Contriever dense retriever selects Cq subset from C (S5.2). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(extraction triggered per incoming query, S3)+PRESUPUESTO(the paper's central contribution IS an explicit, RL-learned, cost-aware BUDGET-TIER router selecting LOW/MID/HIGH per module via reward r=r_task+lambda*alpha*r_cost, Eq.7-10, S4.3). mide_lectura=SI: Table1 measures F1/Judge task performance directly as a function of the extraction/reading budget across LoCoMo/LongMemEval/HotpotQA against 7 strong baselines (ReadAgent/MemoryBank/A-MEM/LangMem/Mem0/MemoryOS/LightMem), e.g. BudgetMem-CAP avg F1 59.99/Judge 61.06 (LLaMA) vs best baseline LightMem 35.45/49.21 at comparable cost -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F, evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E. Fig.2 sweeps performance-cost frontiers across 3 orthogonal tiering strategies (implementation/reasoning/capacity) on LoCoMo -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION;MEDICION-COSTO (cost measured as $ from token usage x service pricing, S5.1). alcance=SESION: primary benchmarks (LoCoMo/LongMemEval) are multi-session dialogue histories; HotpotQA is included as a long-context QA transfer task, not a persistent-scope axis. F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms both facets with no additions needed.
